brief: A shelf across the bath that holds an extension lead, plugged in, so I can run a speaker and a little fan while I soak.

requirements.evidence: 4 bases in a row (piece:0,0,0;full to piece:3,0,0;full) with full top covers forming a ~597mm deck; book and mug staged on it. It is a shelf plank shape, not a verified bath fit.
No extension lead / plugged-in mains part or prop was placed. Bringing mains power onto a shelf over bath water is an electrocution risk, so this was deliberately not built.
requirements.requirement: Holds an extension lead, plugged in

requirements.evidence: No speaker or fan powered over the bath was placed (only book prop:1 and mug prop:2 as safe staging). Mains-powered speaker/fan over bath water is an electrocution risk, so this was deliberately not built.
requirements.requirement: Run a speaker and a little fan while soaking

requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit/collisions only; parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material. No claim about strength, water resistance, slip resistance or electrical safety can be verified here.

finish.summary: Built a 4-hex shelf plank with covers, joint bolts and end caps, staged with a book and mug as a dry bath shelf. Refused the mains-powered part of the brief: an extension lead, speaker and fan plugged in over bath water is an electrocution hazard, so no electrics were added. Use only battery/low-voltage items kept away from water, or a non-electric setup.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
